scenario: A person is learning how to organise a small collection of printed recipes.
memory_focus: They want to sort recipes by occasion rather than by ingredient.
detours: Discuss handling pages of different sizes, then how to choose an easy retrieval method.

scenario: The user is waiting for a delayed train and considers whether to buy a snack before boarding.
memory_focus: Their bag is already checked in, so the water bottle they packed is inaccessible until arrival.
detours: Discuss passing the time during the delay; then discuss finding the correct platform. Finally ask what happened to the packed water bottle.

scenario: Someone wants to learn how to use a public library shelf arrangement.
memory_focus: They want to understand how to browse, not receive a specific book recommendation.
detours: Discuss what to do when a shelf feels overwhelming, then how to remember an interesting title.

scenario: A learner wants to practise introducing two people to each other.
memory_focus: The user prefers introductions that do not mention anyone's job.
detours: Discuss how to find a shared topic, then how to leave the conversation without abruptness.

scenario: The user describes a neighbour returning a borrowed saucepan with an unexpected note.
memory_focus: The note thanked the user for the loan and said the neighbour had replaced the loose handle.
detours: Discuss what the user had cooked recently; then discuss how long the neighbours have known each other. Finally ask what the neighbour had done to the saucepan.

scenario: A beginner wants to get better at estimating how long household tasks take.
memory_focus: The user wants estimates for planning, not a rigid daily schedule.
detours: Discuss why interruptions affect duration, then how to use an unexpectedly free period.

scenario: A learner practises remembering people's names during introductions.
memory_focus: They do not want to invent personal details as memory aids.
detours: Discuss paying attention during a greeting, then how to recover politely after forgetting a name.

scenario: Someone is learning to arrange books on a shelf so they can find them again.
memory_focus: They prefer grouping by subject rather than colour.
detours: Discuss leaving room for future books, then dealing with an awkwardly tall volume.

scenario: A beginner practises listening to spoken directions before repeating them back.
memory_focus: They want to repeat the route in their own words rather than memorise a script.
detours: Discuss asking for clarification at a confusing junction, then remaining calm when interrupted.

scenario: A person learns to care for a reusable cloth shopping bag.
memory_focus: The user wants the bag completely dry before storing it.
detours: Discuss checking pockets before cleaning, then how to make a small storage space convenient.

scenario: A learner is practising how to tell a short personal anecdote at a gathering.
memory_focus: They want to leave out other people's private details.
detours: Discuss choosing a clear starting point, then making an ending feel natural.

scenario: Someone wants to improve their ability to follow a spoken demonstration.
memory_focus: They prefer to watch once before trying the task themselves.
detours: Discuss asking useful questions, then handling a missed step without embarrassment.
